title: A Space Mission Built in a Classroom

paragraphs.en: The students' space club began with a laptop, a telescope, and a blog explaining what they hoped to learn. They could not launch a rocket, but they could build a model of an instrument that might work in orbit. Their teacher asked them to draft a blueprint before purchasing hardware. The framework had to define the mission's purpose, the required input, and the limits of the experiment. Learning science would mean more than assembling an impressive gadget: it would mean making a claim that could survive a careful test.
paragraphs.zh: 学生太空社团最初只有笔记本电脑、望远镜和介绍学习目标的博客。他们无法发射火箭，却可以制作可能在轨道运行的仪器模型。教师要求先画设计图，再购买硬件。框架必须界定任务目标、所需输入和实验限制。学习科学不只是组装先进小装置，而是提出能够经受认真检验的主张。

paragraphs.en: A lesson on geography led to questions about the planet's atmosphere. Why did oxygen support life, and how did chemistry explain the behavior of hydrogen? Students examined a molecule as a system rather than a decorative drawing. They compared the spectrum of light passing through different samples and used a lens to focus a beam onto a sensor. A protective filter prevented excessive brightness, and a measured pulse provided consistent exposure. One team proposed a laser, but the teacher required a risk assessment first. Powerful equipment would not become appropriate merely because it looked sophisticated.
paragraphs.zh: 一堂地理课引出关于地球大气的问题。氧气为何支持生命，化学如何解释氢气的行为？学生把分子当作系统，而不是装饰图案。他们比较光穿过不同样本后的光谱，用透镜将光束聚焦到传感器。保护滤镜防止过强亮度，定量脉冲提供一致曝光。一个团队提议用激光，但教师要求先做风险评估。设备不会仅因看起来先进就适合使用。

paragraphs.en: Mechanical design presented another set of lessons. An aluminum frame reduced weight, while rubber pads protected a delicate circuit from vibration. A cable and a wire carried signals through a narrow tube without tangling. A pump moved fluid between containers, and a valve prevented an acid sample from leaking. Students measured every gram and checked each inch of clearance around moving parts. They studied how a lever and a gear changed force, then learned that a larger momentum made sudden stopping harder. Inertia was no longer just a formula copied from a textbook.
paragraphs.zh: 机械设计带来另一组经验。铝框减重，橡胶垫保护精密电路免受振动。电缆和导线经过狭窄管道输送信号而不缠绕。泵在容器间输送流体，阀门防止酸性样品泄漏。学生测量每克重量，检查活动部件周围每英寸空隙。他们研究杠杆和齿轮如何改变力，再认识到动量更大时突然停下更困难。惯性不再只是从课本抄下的公式。

paragraphs.en: The club also investigated gravity using a curved track. They adjusted the angle, recorded the path of a particle-sized bead, and plotted a curve describing its motion. An astronaut's account reminded them that a laboratory model could not reproduce every dimension of space travel. To reduce waste, they reused fiber insulation and selected a hybrid power supply rather than relying entirely on petrol. A manual documented the design, and an archive stored failed trials as carefully as successful ones. In cyberspace, anonymous praise was plentiful, but evidence required records another team could understand and reproduce.
paragraphs.zh: 社团还用弯曲轨道研究重力。他们调整角度，记录细小颗粒状珠子的路径，并绘制运动曲线。宇航员的叙述提醒他们，实验室模型无法重现太空旅行的每个方面。为减少浪费，他们重复使用纤维保温材料，选择混合供能，而不完全依赖汽油。手册记录设计，档案像保存成功试验一样认真保存失败试验。网络空间里不缺匿名赞扬，但证据需要其他团队能理解并复现的记录。

paragraphs.en: At the final presentation, a failed bulb became the most useful exhibit. It had overheated because the group had assumed a component's advertised rating applied in every environment. Rather than hiding the mistake, they showed how the investigation changed their design and their confidence. The audience learned more from this explanation than from a flawless-looking demonstration. The students had not created a spacecraft. They had acquired habits essential to one: distinguishing a model from reality, testing assumptions before defending them, and treating an unexpected result as an opportunity to understand rather than a reason to pretend.
paragraphs.zh: 最终展示中，烧坏灯泡成为最有用的展品。它过热，是因为小组假设部件宣传的额定值适用于所有环境。他们没有隐藏错误，而是展示调查如何改变设计和信心水平。观众从解释中得到的知识，比看一场貌似无瑕的展示更多。学生没有制造航天器，却获得其所需的习惯：区分模型与现实，先检验再维护假设，以及把意外结果当作理解机会，而不是伪装理由。
